question.prompt: A coin is tossed twice independently. The probability of heads on the first toss is \(1/2\), and the probability of heads on the second toss is \(1/2\). What is the probability of heads on both tosses?

solutions.explanation:
Because the tosses are independent, multiply their heads probabilities:
\[
P(\text{heads on both tosses})=\frac12\cdot\frac12=\frac14.
\]
solutions.title: Multiply independent probabilities

solutions.explanation:
Let \(H\) denote heads and \(T\) denote tails. Since the tosses are independent and each has equally likely heads and tails, the four ordered outcomes
\[
HH,\quad HT,\quad TH,\quad TT
\]
are equally likely. The letters record the first and second toss in order, so the list includes every possibility exactly once. Only \(HH\) has two heads, giving probability \(\frac14\).
solutions.title: List the ordered outcomes
